headline: MALI CRISIS GUTS SYAMA OUTPUT: Resolute Mining Slashes Q2 Gold Guidance 33% on Supply Chain Collapse
snippet: Resolute Mining (ASX: RSG) cut Q2 production guidance at its Syama mine in Mali to just 30,000 ounces — down sharply from 40,000–45,000 oz — after security-related logistical disruptions delayed heavy equipment delivery and cut off explosives supply, forcing the sulphide mill to rely on lower-grade stockpiles. Full-year Syama guidance is now expected at the lower end of 195,000–210,000 oz, with the deferred plant shutdown extended an extra week to mid-June.

headline: SILVER MINER GOES PUBLIC: Sunshine Silver Mining Prices 20M-Share NYSE IPO at $13.50
snippet: Sunshine Silver Mining & Refining (NYSE: SSMR) priced its initial public offering at $13.50 per share, raising approximately $270 million from 20 million shares, with trading on the NYSE commencing June 4 and the offering closing June 5. The company controls major mineral rights in Idaho's Coeur d'Alene Mining District — one of the world's richest historical silver belts — and operates a vertically integrated mine-to-mill-to-refinery platform.

headline: END OF AN ERA: Lynas Rare Earths Names Pol Le Roux Interim CEO as Amanda Lacaze Retires
snippet: Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) announced on June 4 that COO Pol Le Roux will take over as interim CEO on July 1, following the retirement of Amanda Lacaze — the executive who built Lynas from near-insolvency into the world's largest non-Chinese rare earth producer over 14 years. The board is running a permanent CEO search with no fixed timeline, leaving a leadership transition at a company that supplies the majority of the world's separated rare earth oxides outside China.

headline: GOLD DEMAND DROPS BUT PRICES STILL CLIMB 43%: Metals Focus Forecasts $4,920 Average in 2026
snippet: Metals Focus released a 2026 gold market report on June 5 forecasting the annual average gold price will surge 43% to a new record of $4,920 per ounce this year, even as overall gold demand dips from 2025's record levels as investment flows moderate. The firm cited the Middle East conflict, structural central bank buying, and persistent inflation as key price supports, projecting gold finishes 2026 well above current levels near $4,450.

headline: 713 METRES at 2.52 g/t AuEq: DPM Metals Drills Into Porphyry Monster Beside Chelopech Mine
snippet: DPM Metals (ASX: DPM) released drill results from its Brevene South Porphyry target in Bulgaria showing hole EX_BRESPO_03 returned 713 metres grading 2.52 g/t gold equivalent (1.31 g/t Au, 1.16% Cu) from 1,172m depth — with the hole still in progress and encountering intensely mineralised rock at 2,031m. The target sits one kilometre from existing mineral reserves at the adjacent Chelopech operating mine, meaning any resource delineation could directly extend mine life.

headline: RIGS ROLLING IN THE YUKON: Yukon Metals Launches 5,000m Copper-Gold Expedition at AZ and Birch
snippet: Yukon Metals Corp (CSE: YMC) has commenced a fully funded 5,000-metre diamond drill program across its AZ and Birch copper-gold properties in Yukon, Canada — targeting porphyry and skarn mineralization — with first core pulled at AZ on May 28 and rigs now active at both sites. The program (2,000m at AZ, 3,000m at Birch) advances district-scale copper-gold targets through drilling, geophysics, and surface sampling in Canada's most prolific metal belt.

headline: VISIBLE GOLD IN HOLE 1: Metals Creek Hits High-Grade Quartz Veins at Timmins Ogden Project
snippet: Metals Creek Resources (TSXV: MEK) reported visible gold in the first two drill holes at the Ogden Gold Project in Timmins, Ontario — a 50/50 JV operated by MEK with Discovery Silver — with high-grade gold mineralization linked to multiple generations of quartz veins confirmed in both holes. The Timmins camp has produced over 70 million ounces of gold historically, making visible gold from the opening holes a meaningful signal for this joint venture.

headline: THIRD ATTEMPT: Russia Re-Auctions Seized $1.88B Uzhuralzoloto Gold Stake — Bids Due June 9
snippet: Russia launched a third auction for a 67.2% stake in gold producer Uzhuralzoloto (UGC), valued at approximately $1.88 billion, after two consecutive auctions attracted no qualifying bidders — the second failure confirmed May 26. Bids are accepted through June 9 with results due June 10; the stake was seized from businessman Konstantin Strukov under a court nationalization order, part of Russia's broader pattern of corporate asset confiscation since 2022.

headline: DOE BETS $134M ON WASTE-STREAM RARE EARTHS: Louisiana and Oklahoma Projects Greenlit
snippet: The U.S. Department of Energy awarded $134 million to two rare earth extraction projects — roughly $67 million to a Colorado School of Mines/ElementUSA bauxite waste facility in Louisiana targeting 150–1,000 metric tons of rare earths annually, and the remainder to a Phoenix Tailings/MIT demonstration plant in Oklahoma converting industrial waste to high-purity rare earth metals. The awards mark a strategic shift toward waste-stream sourcing to cut U.S. dependence on Chinese rare earth supply chains.

headline: BALD HILL LIVES AGAIN: MinRes Restarts Western Australian Lithium Mine as ASX Producers Slide 4-6%
snippet: Mineral Resources (ASX: MIN) confirmed it will restart its Bald Hill lithium mine in Western Australia, with crushing and mining operations commencing in June and first spodumene concentrate shipment from Esperance expected in Q1 FY27 — even as ASX lithium producers broadly sold off in early June trading, with Pilbara Minerals down 4.4% and Liontown Resources down 6.1%. The restart arrives as energy storage demand for lithium is forecast to surge 55% in 2026, but an estimated 47% of lithium chemical producers remain unprofitable at current prices.
